data.title: bn-3oml: hooks occupy the identity as a rite session attachment of the Claude session
data.description: For bn-3oml: the Claude session-start hook staked an ownerless agent://<name> claim, which rite channel (rite 0.35.0) refuses in the same session. With the hook payload's session_id the hook now runs rite sessions attach --harness claude --kind pull --ttl 600; post-tool-call renews the attachment when its claim has under 120s left (matched by the claim principal session:<attachment>); session-end runs rite sessions detach --session. An attach refused as 'already attached' (compaction re-run, or a rite channel that attached first) is left alone. No session id keeps the ownerless claim. Verified end to end against rite 0.35.0 in a scratch store. Codex has no hooks: its launcher still owns reserve/attach/detach.

data.body: [risk:high] The channel does not take over a hook attachment; it dies. rite channel (0.35.0, src/cli/channel.rs attach_and_renew) attaches under its own session id mcp:<pid> without --replace. When SessionStart wins the race with the MCP handshake, the hook's pull attachment holds agent://<name> and the channel's attach is refused: reproduced in a scratch store, hook first then channel -> channel exit 1, stderr 'rite channel: stopping: cannot take demo-dev: ... demo-dev is already attached to claude session sess-H as attachment ... Pass --replace ... to take over'. Channel first then hook works (hook refusal swallowed, session-end leaves the channel's claim alone). So the bone's symptom (channel refuses the identity in the same session) survives whenever the hook attaches first, and the identity is then held by a pull attachment nothing can push into. Claude Code gives no ordering guarantee between SessionStart hooks and MCP notifications/initialized. Either the channel must replace a same-harness pull attachment (a rite change) or the hook must not attach when a channel is expected for this session; the doc comment on lines 175-185 and the description should not claim the takeover until one of those exists.

[risk:high] 'an attachment is what the channel takes over' is not what rite 0.35.0 does: rite channel attaches without --replace under session mcp:<pid> and exits 1 when the hook's attachment already holds the identity (see the comment on src/hooks/run.rs:186). Reword once the race is settled.

[risk:medium] The 64KB stdin cap now changes behavior. A PostToolUse payload over 64KB (a Read of a large file puts tool_response in the payload) is truncated, serde rejects it, session_id_from returns None, and post-tool-call falls into refresh_claim_if_needed, whose 'claims list --mine' never sees the session-owned claim. Reproduced: attachment with 99s left + 80KB payload -> no renew; same call with a small payload -> renewed to 599s. A run of large tool outputs during the 120s renew window lets the claim lapse (it is recovered on the next small payload because rite reports a lapsed claim as active with negative expires_in_secs, but occupancy shows 'lapsed' meanwhile). Raise the cap (session_id is a few bytes; 1MB is cheap) or pull session_id out without needing the whole document.

[risk:medium] An attach that was refused at SessionStart is never retried. If the identity was held by a stale ownerless claim (previous edict, or a crashed session, up to 10 minutes), or a /clear fires the new SessionStart before the old SessionEnd's detach, session-start reports the refusal and this early return means every later post-tool-call is a no-op: the session runs unoccupied until it ends. attach is idempotent for this session ('already attached' is swallowed), so when attachment_for returns None and rite sessions list shows no live attachment for the agent, post-tool-call could call attach_session again.

[nit] Substring matching on rite's error text conflates two different refusals: 'Session X is already attached to <agent>' (this session, fine to ignore) and '<agent> is already attached to claude session Y ... Pass --replace' (another session holds the identity). The second now passes silently, so a second Claude window started with the same AGENT runs unoccupied with no sign of it. Consider a stderr note for the second case, or check rite sessions list by session id after the refusal instead of parsing the message.

[nit] With rite not on PATH this prints 'edict: could not occupy agent://<name> for this session: running rite' on every session start (stake_claim was silent). Claude Code hides stderr on exit 0 outside debug, so harmless, but the message is unhelpful; skip it when the error is a spawn failure, or say 'rite not found'.

[nit] A session id starting with '-' passes this check and is handed to clap as a flag: {"session_id":"--all"} -> 'rite failed: error: unexpected argument --all'. Harmless (attach fails and is reported), but validate_agent_name rejects a leading '-', and the same rule here keeps the argv shape fixed.

[nit] Tests cover session_id_from but not the two JSON matchers that decide renewal: the attachment lookup (session + attached=true -> attachment_id) and the claim predicate (active, agent == session:<id>, pattern, expires_in_secs < 120). Both are inline with run_command, so they are untestable as written. Extract them as pure fns over serde_json::Value and test with the documented shapes, including a lapsed claim (active=true, expires_in_secs=-1, which must renew) and a claim held by another attachment (must not).

data.reason: Hook-first ordering kills rite channel: the hook's pull attachment holds agent://<name>, rite channel attaches under mcp:<pid> without --replace and exits 1 ('cannot take ... Pass --replace'). Reproduced in a scratch store against rite 0.35.0; see thread on src/hooks/run.rs:186-212. The CHANGELOG's 'an attachment is what the channel takes over' is not true of rite 0.35.0. Also medium: the 64KB stdin cap drops session_id on large PostToolUse payloads so renew is skipped, and a refused attach is never retried.

[risk:low] Once a rite channel has taken the pull attachment over (the intended steady state with rite bn-316s), this session has no live attachment of its own, so every post-tool-call runs 'sessions list' plus a refused 'sessions attach' and prints 'agent://<name> is occupied by another session of this agent; this session is not the occupant.' to stdout on each tool call (reproduced: two consecutive post-tool-calls after the takeover, one line each). Same for a stale ownerless claim: the long 'is held by ... without a session owner' error goes to stderr on every tool call until it expires. Exit 0 keeps it out of Claude's context, so this is transcript noise plus one extra subprocess per call, not an occupancy defect. The sessions list already fetched has the answer: if any attachment of this agent is live under another session, skip the attach quietly (and keep the note for session-start only).
Fixed at a4a27ec2: post-tool-call reads the occupant from the sessions list; another live session of this agent means return quietly, no attach, no note. The note stays on session-start only.
